  "cut_point": "We are given:

- The total length of the road: **10 km**
- The total time allowed: **30 days**
- The number of men initially employed: **30**
- After **10 days**, only **2 km** of the road has been completed.

We are to find the **approximate number of extra men** needed to **finish the work on time**.

---

### Step 1: Understand the work

Let’s define:

- Total work = **10 km**
- Time allowed = **30 days**
- Work done in 10 days = **2 km**

So the **work rate** (work per day) is:

$$
\text{Work rate} = \frac{2 \text{ km}}{10 \text{ days}} = 0.2 \text{ km/day}
$$

This is the **combined work rate** of the 30 men.

---

### Step 2: Find the work rate per man

Let’s assume each man can do **x km/day**.

Then the combined rate of 30 men is:

$$
30x = 0.2 \text{ km/day}
$$

So:

$$
x = \frac{0.2}{30} = \frac{1}{150} \text{ km/day per man}
$$",
